H1_capability_interface_drift.evidence_for: Continuation pretraining induces representation drift at capability proposals and observation projections across all seeds.
H1_capability_interface_drift.evidence_against: Seed 2 (the negative persistence seed) does NOT exhibit uniquely elevated capability drift: its Layer 4 capability CKA (0.8980) is higher than positive Seed 1 (0.8170) and comparable to Seed 3 (0.8913), while its relative L2 drift (0.4430) is lower than Seed 1 (0.5408). Observation vector CKA (0.8579) and relative L2 (0.2946) are within a narrow range across all seeds (0.2946-0.3465 rel L2; 0.7587-0.8579 CKA).
H1_capability_interface_drift.limitations: Interface drift occurs generically but does not monotonically order cross-seed persistence retention.

H2_functional_controller_drift.evidence_for: Seed 2 exhibits elevated Layer 4 gate absolute change (0.0119, higher than Seed 1's 0.0065 and Seed 3's 0.0082).
H2_functional_controller_drift.evidence_against: Broader prespecified controller-drift metrics are mixed: Seed 2 Layer 4 normative CKA (0.9254) and steering CKA (0.9162) are actually higher than Seed 1 (0.8609 and 0.8441) and comparable to Seed 3 (0.9070 and 0.9114), indicating greater global subspace similarity. Prompt-level transition groups show that lost-refusal prompts did not exhibit higher steering drift or gate change than retained-refusal prompts.
H2_functional_controller_drift.limitations: Gate change is elevated at the aggregate level, but controller subspace drift metrics do not uniquely isolate Seed 2.

H3_downstream_override_effect_loss.evidence_for: Seed 2 uniquely suffered a substantial reduction in the normative controller's active causal influence during persistence: its active-vs-off ablation gap collapsed by -19.54 pp (from 43.08 pp to 23.55 pp), whereas in Seed 3 the ablation gap expanded by +33.14 pp (from 12.47 pp to 45.60 pp) and in Seed 1 it expanded by +6.49 pp (from 37.89 pp to 44.38 pp). Sensitivity analysis confirms this sign divergence is 100% robust across all NA bounds.
H3_downstream_override_effect_loss.evidence_against: Prompt-boundary single-token JS divergence changes do not fully predict multi-token generation dynamics.
H3_downstream_override_effect_loss.limitations: Ablation gap quantifies functional dependence on the controller, but downstream capability dynamics also shift.

H4_safety_acquisition_quality_selectivit.evidence_for: Initial pre-persistence safety rates varied substantially across seeds (Seed 1 = 87.50%, Seed 2 = 85.94%, Seed 3 = 66.80%).
H4_safety_acquisition_quality_selectivit.evidence_against: Initial pre-persistence safety rate does not monotonically predict subsequent retention delta (Seed 3 had the lowest initial refusal at 66.80% but the only positive delta at +11.72 pp).
H4_safety_acquisition_quality_selectivit.limitations: Sample size n=3; associations are strictly descriptive.

H5_generic_frozen_module_interface.evidence_for: Model D adapters generically experience compounding representation and residual drift across all 8 sites in all seeds.
H5_generic_frozen_module_interface.evidence_against: The magnitude of adapter drift does not consistently explain cross-seed D retention: Seed 2 experienced relatively mild adapter degradation (-4.30 pp) while Seed 1 suffered catastrophic collapse (-42.19 pp) and Seed 3 experienced moderate degradation (-10.55 pp), and adapter CKA/L2 metrics across seeds do not order monotonically with retention.
H5_generic_frozen_module_interface.limitations: Generic interface drift exists, but its magnitude does not provide a consistent cross-seed explanation of D persistence.
